citations.claim: pole exceeded 0.8 rad limit at first violating step 43 (theta 0.86, margin -0.06) with high energy 37.56
three steps before failure energy already elevated to 24.36 showing runaway growth
earlier at step 35 energy was 8.23, showing progressive destabilization from small initial energy 1.46

counterfactual.change: set sensor_noise from 0.01524 to 0, keeping all else identical; noisy angle feedback was driving destabilizing control, so clean sensing restores balance

explanation: Shrunk scenario has sensor_noise ~0.015 on pole-angle measurement with no pushes. Controller acts on corrupted angle feedback, applying incorrect forces (e.g., ~36.8N at step 35, ~42.9N at step 40) that pump energy (1.46 initial to 8.2 at step 35 to 24.4 at step 40 to 37.6 at step 43) instead of stabilizing. Pole swings from near-upright to 0.86 rad by step 43, violating pole_upright. Removing noise alone prevents failure, confirming noisy feedback as cause.
vision_note: The pole tilts progressively farther to the right from step 40 through step 42 while the cart stays near the center of the track. By step 43 the pole tip is highlighted red at a large angle from vertical, marking the upright violation.
